components.name: field
components.description: A label, description and error wrapper for an explicitly identified control.
components.accessibility: The for prop must equal the nested control id. Also set required on the control. When using description/error, provide descriptionId/errorId and pass those same ids to the nested control describedby prop (space-separated if both). Mark the control invalid=true for an error. IDs must be unique in the document.

<ui:field for="contact-name" label="Your name" t:bind-required="true">

</ui:field>

components.name: input
components.description: A native single-line input with label/error association.
components.accessibility: Always provide a visible associated label. Placeholder is not a label. Pass a unique id for each repeated control. File inputs do not gain upload capability from this component.
components.template: <input class="portal-input" t:attr-id="props.id" t:attr-name="props.name" t:attr-type="props.type" t:attr-value="props.value" t:attr-placeholder="props.placeholder" t:attr-disabled="props.disabled" t:attr-required="props.required" t:attr-readonly="props.readonly" t:attr-aria-invalid="props.invalid" t:attr-aria-describedby="props.describedby" t:attr-autocomplete="props.autocomplete" t:attr-inputmode="props.inputmode" t:attr-min="props.min" t:attr-max="props.max" t:attr-step="props.step"/>

<ui:input id="email-example" name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email" placeholder="you@example.com">
</ui:input>

components.name: textarea
components.description: A native multiline control.
components.accessibility: Always provide a visible associated label. The value is text content, not an HTML value attribute.
components.template: <textarea class="portal-textarea" t:attr-id="props.id" t:attr-name="props.name" t:attr-rows="props.rows" t:attr-placeholder="props.placeholder" t:attr-disabled="props.disabled" t:attr-required="props.required" t:attr-readonly="props.readonly" t:attr-aria-invalid="props.invalid" t:attr-aria-describedby="props.describedby" t:attr-autocomplete="props.autocomplete" t:text="props.value"/>

<ui:textarea id="notes-example" name="notes">
</ui:textarea>

components.name: select
components.description: A native select with caller-owned option elements.

components.name: icon

Icons follow currentColor, mirror their direction on right-to-left pages and stay visible in forced-colours mode.

components.description: A fieldset of large, selectable option cards backed by native radios.
components.accessibility: A real fieldset and legend group the choices, and each card is a native radio inside its label: arrow keys move between options and the form submits without JavaScript. The selected card adds a border and an inset ring as well as a tint. Give every option-card in the group the same name.

components.description: One selectable option inside option-cards: a native radio with a label, description and aside.
components.accessibility: The radio stays a native input inside its label, so the whole card is the click target and the name, description and aside are read together. A component cannot read its parent's props, so pass the shared name on every card. Disabled options stay visible and are skipped by the keyboard.

components.name: quantity-input
components.description: A native number input with enhancement-only − and + buttons.
components.accessibility: The number input is the control: it is labelled, typeable, honours min, max and step and submits without JavaScript. The runtime quantity behaviour reveals the − and + buttons, which carry translatable aria-labels and fire native input and change events. Validate the quantity again on the server.

components.name: basket-line
components.description: One basket or order line with media, details, actions and a line total; with a line it updates or removes itself.
components.accessibility: Each line is an article headed by an h3 with the product name, so screen-reader users can move line by line. Totals are preformatted by the server. With line, the row shows a labelled quantity input and Update and Remove buttons whose accessible names include the product name (visually hidden), so repeated rows stay distinct. Privileged: those buttons run the site's lib/basket.lua, which must check that the line belongs to the visitor. Without line, put edit and remove actions in the actions slot, with the same context.

line.description: The basket line this row edits. With it, the row shows a quantity control and Update and Remove buttons, handled by the site's lib/basket.lua.

components.description: A buy-it-now button with a quantity, handing the visitor to the site's checkout.
components.accessibility: The quantity is a labelled native number input and the button a real submit button, so it works without JavaScript and from the keyboard; Enter in the quantity submits. The button's accessible name includes the product name (visually hidden), so several on one page stay distinct. Errors render in a role="alert" region. Privileged: its server export runs the site's lib/checkout.lua with the visitor's Portal access and may redirect to an https checkout page.

product.description: What the button buys. Its id reaches the checkout module signed, so a visitor cannot swap it.

price.description: The price shown above the button, formatted by the server.

Build rows with description-list so terms and values stay associated. Totals are calculated on the server; never present a client-side estimate as the payable amount.

    <ui:link href="#basket">Back to basket</ui:link>
  </ui:fill>
</ui:order-summary>

components.name: dialog
components.description: A native modal dialog with a trigger, title, body and footer.
components.accessibility: Uses a native dialog opened with showModal, so focus moves into it, the page behind is inert, Escape closes it and focus returns to the trigger. Supporting browsers handle the trigger and close button through invoker commands; the runtime dialog behaviour covers the rest. The trigger is enhancement-only: without JavaScript it stays hidden, so keep an ordinary page link to the same content. The trigger slot is the label inside the component's own button; the close button is labelled by closeLabel.

  <ui:description-item term="Finish">
    <ui:badge t:bind-dot="true" variant="primary">Soft-touch laminate</ui:badge>
  </ui:description-item>
</ui:description-list>

components.name: timeline
components.description: An ordered progress timeline of done, current and upcoming steps.
components.accessibility: An ordered list labelled by label, so its length and position are announced. The current step carries aria-current="step", and every step starts with visually hidden state text (Completed, Current step, Upcoming), so state never relies on the marker colour or icon. Markers are decorative and mirror on right-to-left pages.
components.style:
/* Status: timeline, stat, estimate and files */
.portal-timeline { display: grid; margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; }
components.usage:
<ui:timeline label="Order PF-1042 progress">
  <ui:timeline-step title="Order received" state="done" time="Mon 09:12"/>
  <ui:timeline-step title="Proof approved" state="done" time="Mon 14:40">
    Approved by Amira Hassan.
  </ui:timeline-step>
  <ui:timeline-step title="Printing" state="current" time="Today">
    On press 2, 400gsm matt.
  </ui:timeline-step>
  <ui:timeline-step title="Dispatched" time="Est. Thu"/>
</ui:timeline>

components.name: timeline-step
components.description: One step in a timeline: a title, an optional time and detail.
components.accessibility: Renders a list item. state=current adds aria-current="step". The state is spelled out as visually hidden text before the title; pass stateLabel to translate it (for example "Erledigt:"). Use only inside timeline.
components.usage:
<ui:timeline label="Reprint progress">
  <ui:timeline-step title="Artwork checked" state="done" time="09:30" stateLabel="Erledigt:"/>
  <ui:timeline-step title="Druckplattenbelichtung und Farbabstimmung" state="current" time="Heute"/>
  <ui:timeline-step title="Ready for collection"/>
</ui:timeline>

components.name: stat
components.description: A labelled key figure with an optional change and trend.
components.accessibility: The label precedes the value in reading order. The trend arrow is decorative and coloured as a supplement: the change text must say the direction and amount itself (for example "+3 this week"). Values are preformatted by the server.
components.usage:
<ui:grid columns="3">
  <ui:stat label="Open orders" value="12" change="+3 this week" trend="up"/>
  <ui:stat label="Average turnaround" value="2.4 days" change="−0.3 days" trend="down"/>
  <ui:stat label="Spend this year" value="£184.250.000,00" change="Same as last year" trend="flat"/>
</ui:grid>

components.name: estimate-panel
components.description: A price estimate with line rows, a total that can follow a quantity live, delivery and actions.
components.accessibility: Renders a section with an h2 title and the total as a dt/dd pair. With unitPrice, a control named quantity inside the panel re-estimates the total as the visitor edits it: only the total is replaced, never the control being edited, and without JavaScript the total stays as rendered. Announce updates from a data-portal-status outlet outside the panel. The estimate is not a quote: the server recalculates the payable price.

unitPrice.description: Price of one item. With it, the total follows the quantity control live.

currency.description: Written before a live total, for example £.

components.usage:
<ui:estimate-panel total="£42.00" t:bind-unitPrice="0.084" currency="£" delivery="Arrives Thursday 13 November">
  <ui:fill name="status">
    <ui:badge variant="success" t:bind-dot="true">In stock</ui:badge>
  </ui:fill>
  <ui:quantity-input id="estimate-quantity" name="quantity" label="Business cards" t:bind-value="500" t:bind-step="50" t:bind-min="50"/>
  <ui:description-list layout="inline">
    <ui:description-item term="Price per card">8.4p</ui:description-item>
  </ui:description-list>
  <ui:fill name="actions">
    <ui:button t:bind-disabled="true">Add to basket</ui:button>
  </ui:fill>
</ui:estimate-panel>

components.name: file-list
components.description: A list of downloadable files.
components.accessibility: A list of ordinary links. Each link names the file, then its type and size, so the accessible name says what will download and how big it is. Serve files through an authorised page or Folder route; the link grants no access by itself.
components.style:
.portal-file-list { display: grid; margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; }
.portal-file-list { border: 1px solid var(--_hairline); border-radius: var(--portal-radius); background: var(--portal-surface); overflow: clip; }
components.usage:
<ui:file-list>
  <ui:file-item href="#invoice-pf-1042" name="Invoice PF-1042.pdf" type="PDF" size="84 KB"/>
  <ui:file-item href="#proof-pf-1042" name="Approved proof, business cards, version 3.pdf" type="PDF" size="2.4 MB"/>
  <ui:file-item href="#delivery-note" name="Delivery note"/>
</ui:file-list>

components.name: file-item
components.description: One downloadable file inside file-list: name, type and size.
components.accessibility: An ordinary link with the download attribute; the icons are decorative. Use only inside file-list.
components.usage:
<ui:file-list>
  <ui:file-item href="#artwork-guide" name="Artwork guide.pdf" type="PDF" size="1.2 MB"/>
</ui:file-list>

components.name: code-block
components.description: Preformatted code with a language label and a copy button.
components.accessibility: The code sits in a pre that is keyboard-focusable, so long lines can be scrolled with the arrow keys, and stays left-to-right on right-to-left pages. language is a visible label only: there is no client-side highlighting. With copy (the default) the runtime copy behaviour reveals the button, copies the text and announces copiedMessage (default "Copied"; set it alongside copyLabel to localise the control); without JavaScript the button stays hidden and the text stays selectable. Write the code flush to the start of the line: whitespace in the slot is preserved.
components.usage:
<ui:code-block language="Shell">curl https://print.example/api/v1/orders/PF-1042 \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $PAPER_AND_FORM_KEY"</ui:code-block>

components.name: endpoint
components.description: An API operation heading: method, path, summary and documentation content.
components.accessibility: Renders a section headed by an h3 that reads as method then path, for example "GET /v1/orders/{reference}". The method colour comes from the status tokens and is never the only cue: the method is always written out. Paths stay left-to-right and wrap at any character instead of overflowing.
components.usage:
<ui:endpoint method="GET" path="/v1/orders/{reference}" summary="Retrieve one order with its line items and production status."/>
<ui:endpoint method="POST" path="/v1/orders" summary="Place an order from an accepted estimate."/>
<ui:endpoint method="DELETE" path="/v1/customers/{customerReference}/delivery-addresses/{addressReference}/default-preferences"/>

components.name: property-table
components.description: A table of API or schema properties: name, type, required and description.
components.accessibility: A captioned table with real column headers (translatable through the *Label props). Supply one tr per property with four td cells; write "Yes" or "No" for Required rather than a symbol. The labelled wrapper is keyboard-focusable so a wide table can be scrolled.
components.style:
.portal-table-wrap .portal-property-table td:first-child code { font-weight: var(--_portal-weight-medium); white-space: nowrap; }
.portal-table-wrap .portal-property-table td:nth-child(2) { color: var(--portal-text-muted); font-family: var(--portal-font-mono); font-size: .8125rem; }
components.usage: reference string Yes Your order reference, for example PF-1042. status string Yes One of received, proofing, printing, dispatched or delivered. deliveryNote string or null No Instructions for the courier.

components.name: key-display
components.description: A labelled secret that shows only its masked form and copies the full value. The full value is delivered in the page source as a hidden copy source, so use it only on authenticated pages shown to the key's owner.
components.accessibility: Only masked is displayed or announced: the full value sits in a hidden copy source, so it never appears on screen or in the accessibility tree, and the copy button (revealed by the runtime copy behaviour) puts it on the clipboard and announces copiedMessage (default "Copied"; set it alongside copyLabel to localise the control). The full value is delivered in the page source (the hidden copy source), so anyone who can view the source of the page has the key: use it only on authenticated, uncached pages shown to the key's owner, mask on the server, and prefer showing a new secret once.

components.name: avatar
components.description: A round image or initials standing for a person or organisation.
components.accessibility: The avatar is an image named by name; initials and any photo inside it are hidden from assistive technology. DataXML cannot derive initials, so the caller passes them. When the name is already written next to the avatar, prefer leaving the avatar out of the reading order in your own markup.
components.usage:
<ui:stack direction="horizontal" align="center">
  <ui:avatar name="Amira Hassan" initials="AH" size="sm"/>
  <ui:avatar name="Jonas Müller-Lüdenscheidt" initials="JM"/>
  <ui:avatar name="Paper & Form studio" initials="P&F" size="lg"/>
</ui:stack>

components.name: kbd
components.description: A keyboard key or shortcut, styled as a keycap.
components.accessibility: Uses the native kbd element. Write key names out in full where they are ambiguous (for example "Ctrl"), and never make a shortcut the only way to do something.
components.template:
<kbd class="portal-kbd">
  <ui:outlet name="default"/>
</kbd>
components.style: .portal-kbd { display: inline-block; min-inline-size: 1.75em; padding-inline: .375em; border: 1px solid var(--_hairline); border-block-end-width: 2px; border-radius: .375em; background: var(--portal-surface); color: var(--portal-text); font-size: .8125em; line-height: 1.6; text-align: center; }
components.usage: Press Ctrl + K to search orders.

layouts.name: layout-shop
layouts.title: Print shop
layouts.description: A public storefront: a branded hero, a bestseller grid and a product page with paper options, quantity and a live estimate.
layouts.integration: Load products and prices with a read loader and pass server-formatted amounts to price. Put the options and quantity in a GET form targeting the estimate region (data-portal-region on the wrapper, data-portal-live on the form) with a status outlet outside it; recalculate the estimate in Lua on every change. Adding to the basket is a protected Lua action. The product band is plain section markup rather than the section component because a region cannot sit inside a component slot. This static example has no form, so nothing is calculated or submitted. The product illustrations under /examples/images/ exist only in this showcase: replace them with your own asset URLs.

layouts.name: layout-api
layouts.title: API reference
layouts.description: Developer documentation: endpoints with parameter tables, copyable code samples in tabs and a masked API key with a copy button.
layouts.integration: Generate endpoints and property tables from your API description in Lua and pass tabs from loader data. Render key-display only on authorised, uncached pages, mask the key on the server and pass the full value only to the signed-in owner; prefer showing a new secret once. Copy buttons and tabs need the Portal runtime; without it every sample still shows. The key here is fictional.

Paper & Form Developers Guides API reference Changelog Dashboard

    Authentication

    Send your secret key as a bearer token and keep it on your server. Test keys never print or charge.

    curl https://print.example/v1/orders \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $PAPER_AND_FORM_KEY"
